````markdown
## Proven, unproven and newly proposed work

### Accepted small-model path

Qwen3.5 original GGUF0.8B and2B CPU/resident CUDA, independent sessions,
full-vocabulary/all42-domain comparisons, native row bands2/4/8, ragged
frontiers, refill, device greedy feedback and physical cancellation/retirement
are accepted only within the recorded profiles, context capacities and tests.
GPU context beyond the qualified512 consumed-token scope is open.

At `fb68d8f`, the row/scatter certification phase passed46 physical
model/owner/private-graph/failure cases,10 operator/failure cases, full
isolated1251-test gate, relevant strict checks and both original release
routes, plus14 worker and12 HTTP cases. Its native-only paired comparison
completed144 measured requests/1152 tokens across32 processes: observed
C8 raw token rates improved about1.7%; C1 was nearly unchanged.
These historical executions are not rerun or extended by this handoff.

### Numerical issue

There is **no demonstrated single recurrence algebra bug** accounting for all
differences. Fresh first64 default-versus-AR1 comparisons locate:

- .8B: layer3 attention AV at position2, before the old layer4 GDN boundary.
- 2B: layer0 F32 alpha projection at position0; beta differs before recurrence.
- Default tinyBLAS and AR1 use different FP32 partial-accumulator/reduction
  schedules; later2B Q8 dequantized BLAS versus activation-quantized dots is
  a separate route difference.

Fresh8K AR1 and explicit `use_ref` controls already match the accepted Rust
profile. The old historical raw corpus is unrecovered. Do not call the old
issue closed merely because a new corpus passes; do not call all8K wrong.

Latest source investigation identifies further **profile differences** with
pinned vLLM: fused conv activation/store, prefill versus decode Q/K casts,
FP32 beta, scale placement, fused gated norm and mixed-precision chunk64/WY.
The old diagnostic also unconditionally rounds a weighted gamma product where
raw-F32-gamma CPU arithmetic should promote. The detailed arithmetic audit
and reviewed15-finding plan are preserved in full.

Source inspection alone has not identified the first actual full-model
vLLM→Rust mismatch or proven that changing those operations closes it.
Effective loaded dtypes, GGUF loader log/exp transforms, temporary activation
quantizers and selected compiled routes must be compared first.

### Original HF and27B

The common typed engine already has many genuine trained CPU operator
qualifications. Additional cached H48, BF16-gamma and wide-role results
exist in the isolated ROOT tree; they are not merged whole-model support.
Initial chunk, live coefficients, native-exp/provider admission, full trained
producer composition and complete112-domain/logit parity remain open.

Original27B has about55.56GB of BF16 weight bytes; it does not fit the local
6GiB GPU or the current bounded benchmark process configuration.
Source windows are not yet full streamed inference. Do not bypass executable
source, full-K projection or physical memory limits to claim support.

### Actual vLLM comparisons

Pinned vLLM0.31+cu129
`db9527a46873454610df6dbedf79a36d6bf1a7f6`, Torch2.13+cu129 and official
GGUF plugin `e2b8ad532b8b5ea175100202c30430c1d2b5e6a8` ran genuine comparisons.

|2B|14.540s|1.562s|

These are bounded cold-process eager C1 results. Source-loaded arithmetic

prompt is not numerical qualification. Warm/default/concurrent matched

kernels; stock's9,318 recorded activities do not have proven complete/lossless

## Working and verification rules

Use one Rust mathematical engine, immutable SourceIdentity, one
TaskCoordinator/SessionAuthority root publication authority, the original
ResourceArbiter and physical GPU queue/lease/event/quarantine ownership.
No separate model engine, false Ready, metadata-only execution claim,
post-launch fallback or cross-session writable state aliasing.

Implementation acceptance requires focused tests, relevant strict Clippy,
real source/state/cancellation/physical CUDA gates and both approved original
cache-direct/HF-import release parity routes. Those import routes do not
themselves qualify complete original-HF BF16 inference. Complete gate:

```sh
CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 RAYON_NUM_THREADS=4 python3 scripts/native-gpu.py -- bash scripts/check.sh
```

The native isolation wrapper and rootless Podman have different namespaces.
Do not run full rootless Podman inside the wrapper's single-UID mapping.
Reuse the retained approved private-loopback/owned-process helper, record-only
signal guard and exact source/env binding when runtime work is resumed.
No asynchronous exception across process creation; no reap-then-kill of a
possibly recycled process group. Unknown device completion retains ownership.

When merging from worktrees, use fresh file modification times; preserving
old timestamps previously allowed stale Cargo libraries. Verify the actual
artifact/profile before treating a `target/release` executable as accepted.

No runtime tests were run to create this handoff. Documentation validation
does not extend any numerical, device, model, serving or performance claim.
````

````markdown
Latest target differences, source-proven but not all captured as causal failures:

- GGUF accepted codecs prepare Q8_0/Q8_1/Q8_K activations by source codec;
  stock plugin uses Q8_1 plus its own rounding/scales/reducer/cast path.

  Ordinary norm subtracts1; GDN raw gamma is excluded. Loaded-parameter adapters
  and grouped permutations belong in the declared target profile.
- vLLM fused conv applies SiLU to F32 accumulation before its BF16 store;
  CPU original conv stores BF16 before separate SiLU. Neither is an arbitrary bug.
- SM86 automatic prefill selects Triton; ordinary packed decode uses
  `_forward_core_decode_non_spec`, not the guarded C++ MTP path merely because
  GDN_DECODE_KERNEL says cuda. Actual branch/environment must be observed.
- Prefill Q/K normalization stores BF16; beta/log gates stay F32. Cached normal
  decode works in F32 and scales Q before readout. Prefill and decode softplus
  expressions differ. FLA_USE_FAST_OPS and FLA_TRIL_PRECISION matter.
- CUDA chunk64 is mixed-precision WY/solve_tril: source16×16 block solve/merge,
  BF16 solved-A/u/w/saved entering h/v_new boundaries, F32 running state, explicit
  causal masks and dot policies. Do not substitute CPU six-BMM/STRSM schedule.
- vLLM gated norm retains F32 through gamma/SiLU to finalBF16; CPU raw-F32/BF16
  gamma contracts have their own qualified boundaries.
````

````markdown
# Pinned vLLM GDN arithmetic audit

Author: `/root/spine_review`; 2026-10-20. Parent: `numerics-and-context` and
`model-execution`. Investigation/planning only. No implementation, compilation,
tests, imports, model/operator/provider execution or weight/binary/DSO scans.
Only this owned run is written; paused SASS/SiLU work is untouched.

## Decision

Use the pinned vLLM CUDA GDN path as the target. Port its operation graph,
storage boundaries and head mapping into the existing mathematical engine.
Keep the accepted GGUF/GGML CPU schedule and the independently qualified Torch
CPU helpers explicit; their different arithmetic is intentional source behavior.

The first **source-proven postprojection mismatch** against vLLM is convolution
finalization in `crates/zerogravity/src/original_qwen_math.rs:806–813`: the old
diagnostic stores BF16 raw convolution, then applies SiLU and stores BF16 again.
vLLM's CUDA convolution applies SiLU to its FP32 accumulator and stores BF16
once. This statement assumes identical projection results and prior convolution
history. It is not evidence that convolution is the first actual trained-model
divergence: input norm/projection arithmetic can already differ.

Next concrete differences: vLLM beta stays FP32; prefill stores normalized Q/K
as BF16; normal decode keeps normalized Q/K in FP32 and scales Q before readout;
its fused gated RMS keeps normalization, gamma and SiLU multiplication FP32
until one BF16 output. The old diagnostic does not implement those boundaries.

No algebraic state-orientation/head-repeat bug was found in the inspected Rust
AR recurrence. There is no source basis for globally replacing its accepted
GGUF schedule or for treating all existing CPU numerical differences as bugs.

Notation: `HK` key/query heads; `HV` value heads; `K` key width; `Vd` value width;
`r = HV/HK`; `R_B` BF16 round-to-nearest-even storage; `S[h,v,k]` recurrent state.

actual cache dtype separately. Norm epsilon is `config.rms_norm_eps` via

CPU slow HF promotes Q/K to F32 and uses its own `rsqrt` sequence; no BF16 Q/K store there. |
| Decode Q/K | Conv BF16 → FP32; `q / sqrt(sum(q*q)+1e-6)` and same for K; **remain FP32**. Packed kernel `317–320`. | GGUF uses RMS(`eps/K`) then scale `1/sqrt(K)`, with separate rounded F32 operations and a different reduction. Algebraic equivalence does not imply equal bits. |

Closed CPU helpers retain those distinctions. The old diagnostic rounds weighted gamma even when F32 gamma would promote, so it is not a complete CPU-profile implementation either. |

### Exact normal packed-decode recurrence

The following is an operation-level transcription of
`fused_recurrent.py:291–344`, not a portable host implementation or a claim
about the final compiled instructions. Every arithmetic temporary is FP32.

```text
hq = floor(hv / (HV/HK))
q,k,v = widen_BF16(conv_silu_qkv slices)
q = q / sqrt(reduce_sum(q*q) + 1e-6)
k = k / sqrt(reduce_sum(k*k) + 1e-6)
q = q * (K**-0.5)
x = widen(a[hv]) + widen(dt_bias[hv])
sp = select(x <= 20, log(1 + exp(x)), x)
g = -exp(widen(A_log[hv])) * sp
beta = sigmoid(widen(b[hv]))
S[v,k] = S[v,k] * exp(g)
residual[v] = v[v] - reduce_sum_k(S[v,k] * k[k])
delta[v] = residual[v] * beta
S[v,k] = S[v,k] + delta[v] * k[k]
o[v] = reduce_sum_k(S[v,k] * q[k])
store_BF16(o); store_configured_cache_dtype(S)
```

`exp(g)` in this kernel uses `ops/op.py`'s alias: `tl.exp` by default,
`tldevice.fast_expf` if `FLA_USE_FAST_OPS=1`. Its coefficient `exp(A_log)`,
softplus `exp/log` and sigmoid are direct Triton operations in the kernel.
Do not silently equate these with SLEEF, glibc, MKL VML or host Rust `exp`.

**Contraction/reduction uncertainty:** Triton expressions allow compiler fusion
and determine a device reduction tree; they do not independently prove the
exact FMA count, multiply rounding, instruction selection or exp approximation
of a CubeCL rewrite. The accepted Rust GGML helper explicitly uses `mul_add`
and its SIMD/FMA dot tree. Reusing that helper would import a different schedule.
An actual pinned vLLM operator replay plus compiled-kernel inspection is needed
before asserting instruction-exact parity. No private ABI or host-expression
fit is proposed.

### Exact prefill/initial chunk boundaries

Source: `ops/chunk.py:35–99`, `chunk_scaled_dot_kkt.py:90–122`,
`wy_fast.py:75–137`, `chunk_delta_h.py:93–313,367–371`,
`chunk_o.py:101–162`. Chunk size is 64 (`ops/utils.py:31`).

1. Prepare normalized Q/K/V in BF16, beta/log-gate in FP32 as above.
2. FP32 chunk-local cumulative log-gate `G = cumsum(g)`.
3. Strict-lower system `A_ij = beta_i * dot(k_i,k_j) * exp(G_i-G_j)`;
   CUDA source retains promoted FP32 beta-scaled dot operands, outputs FP32.
4. `solve_tril` returns inverse/solved representation **in K dtype BF16**.
   Its FP32 block-merge dot precision is separately selected by
   `FLA_TRIL_PRECISION` (`solve_tril.py:22–26`): default `ieee`, CUDA also
   permits `tf32`/`tf32x3`. Record this setting; it is not implicit in BF16
   output storage. The solved representation is the inverse of `I + A_lower`.
5. Recompute `u` and `w` with BF16 operands/results: beta-scaled V and
   beta/exp-scaled K explicitly cast BF16 before dot; outputs BF16.
6. Chunk state accumulator remains FP32 `[HV,Vd,K]`. Initial state is either
   exact prior or zero according to metadata. Save each chunk's entering state
   as **BF16 h**. Compute `v_new = u - w @ h`; store BF16 v_new. Apply chunk
   decay to FP32 state; cast decay-adjusted delta BF16 before its K/delta dot
   update. Final recurrent state buffer is FP32.
7. Output uses BF16 Q/K/h/v_new dots, FP32 accumulators and causal mask;
   gated attention coefficients cast BF16 before the V dot. Scale both output
   terms, add, then BF16 output store.

This is not merely an AR loop batched in time. A clean port must preserve the
actual mixed-precision WY graph, including the triangular-solve output dtype,
or explicitly stop short of claiming prefill parity. The original CPU slow
fallback instead promotes the whole graph to F32 and uses public Torch
triangular solves (`H:337–430`); its accepted captures remain a separate target.

## Immutable GGUF source transformation is part of the profile

Plugin `weights_adapter/qwen3_5.py:43–65,188–203,282–349`:

- GGUF `ssm_a` contains negative exponentiated decay: stock loader reconstructs
  vLLM `A_log` using `torch.log(-weight)`. Re-exp later need not reproduce the
  original stored GGUF bits. Record the loaded tensor, not only raw source kind.
- Ordinary norm weights subtract one for vLLM's zero-centered loader convention;
  GDN norm gamma is excluded from that transform.
- If `HV/HK>1`, restore tiled V/Z/A/B/conv-V/dt/A_log head rows. Q/K rows stay
  in their existing order. Dense out-projection columns can be restored;
  packed quantized columns cannot be permuted as ordinary scalar columns.
  The latter use `GGUFHeadTilingLayout.input_to_gguf` at runtime.
- `quantization/layout.py:49–91` maps stored repeat-major/group-major head tiles
  to contiguous per-key-head groups and inversely maps the output activation.
  For the approved small models `HV==HK`, this particular head tiling is absent;
  for 27B grouped heads it must be explicit.
- Identical GGUF weights do not imply identical projection arithmetic:
  Zerogravity activation preparation uses Q8_0/Q8_1/Q8_K by codec, while the
  plugin's quantized path uses its own Q8_1/native kernels and cast policy.
  A first GDN comparison should feed both cores the **same captured actual
  projection operands/results**, then qualify the projection route separately.

Actual accepted vLLM original-HF loaded-cast profile previously audited by ROOT
is also distinct: A_log F32; GDN gamma BF16. Neither the CPU official-all-BF16
profile nor the restored-36-F32 profile is that loaded GPU profile. Full-model
claims must bind the chosen loaded source/cast behavior, not infer it from
checkpoint metadata.

## Minimal directly portable work and fastest gates

No implementation is authorized now. Recommended sequence inside the existing
engine once resumed:

1. **One layer0 GDN-core golden from the pinned actual vLLM route.** Capture
   postprojection QKV/Z/A/B, original raw conv history/weights, loaded A_log/dt/
   gamma, conv+SiLU, normalized Q/K, beta/g/gain, entering/proposed state, core
   and gated output. First initial prefill and then genuine cached decode,
   teachers 11→353. Compare plain versus observed full logits/state first.
   This localizes real divergence and avoids changing exponentials first when
   an earlier cast boundary is already wrong.
2. **Port the narrow conv+SiLU and post-conv preparation operation graph.**
   Same PlanBuilder/backend/source leases; FP32 activation until BF16 output;
   prefill/decode Q/K boundaries explicit. Preserve CPU helper semantics under
   `TorchCpuBf16Avx2MixedSourceV1` instead of widening that profile to CUDA.
   A distinct execution profile in the existing enum is enough; no new engine.
3. **Port normal cached recurrence and fused norm.** Canonical `[HV,Vd,K]`
   state, contiguous Q/K head replication, FP32 beta/decay, pre-scaled Q and
   final casts from the table. Original SessionAuthority/Ready/leases publish
   exactly as before. Qualify zero/nonzero prior independently; verify every
   state word and output, not just generated text.
4. **Port the actual chunk64 WY graph** with its BF16 intermediates, then qualify
   lengths 1/2/63/64/65 and continued nonzero prior. Equal mathematics alone
   cannot justify replacing it with the accepted CPU AR/slow chunk schedule.
5. Full layer/full model only after the narrow core plus projection/norm route
   agree with actual vLLM; then full vocabulary and all independently owned
   state domains, cancellation/Ready discard/unknown completion tests.

Meaningful narrow tests:

- Convolution inputs crossing a BF16 rounding boundary before SiLU: genuine
  fused vLLM output must distinguish one final store from the old two-store
  diagnostic. Keep raw state history bit-exact.
- Nonzero beta showing F32 coefficient versus prematurely BF16-rounded beta;
  negative/positive softplus and threshold20 cases in each actual route.
- Q/K zero, very small values, nontrivial sums; enforce fixed `1e-6` and the
  prefill BF16/decode FP32 distinction. Do not substitute model RMS epsilon.
- `HK=2,HV=6` head sentinels prove `[0,0,0,1,1,1]` Q/K grouping; roundtrip only
  the proper GGUF V/head rows and quantized-output activation layout.
- Signed/nonuniform state and Q expose scale-before-reduction and state-axis
  errors; checking only all-zero prior would hide both.
- Gated RMS example where BF16 gamma multiplication differs from an FP32
  product before gating, paired with the existing CPU counterexample. Expected
  vLLM bits come from the actual public kernel, not the proposed port.

License for any later source port: retain vLLM Apache-2.0 notices. Vendored FLA
files additionally identify the original MIT code and copyright
`Songlin Yang, Yu Zhang (2023–2025)`; retain that original notice/license too.
The plugin's source has the vLLM Apache-2.0 contributor notice. This audit copies
no implementation into production.

- Not proven here: actual selected runtime branch/environment, compiled
  contraction/reduction topology, per-operator vLLM→Rust numerical parity, or
  first causal trained-model difference. No model/operator was executed.
- Prior CPU/GGUF exact receipts stay valid within their own declared schedules;
  they are not vLLM CUDA evidence. Existing owning TODOs remain authoritative.
````

````markdown
### B5–B8 serving semantics that must survive optimization

- GeneratedText GPU presentation stages a token once and resumes only pending
  bounded transport events. If final Text queues but Done is blocked, retry
  cannot duplicate Text, token usage or terminal. CPU accept remains fail-closed.
- A per-packet presented mark survives discarded candidate retries. Presentation
  precedes packet feedback. Blocked output rows park with bounded timeout and
  are excluded from GPU feedback; cancellation/disconnection retires them.
- Actual B1-produced→native and native-produced→B1 packet handoffs are tested.
  Genuine trained EOS, unequal output limits, after-Ready cancellation,
  capacity1 backpressure, survivor replay and final active/queue/failed0 pass.
- Native widths2/4/8 are ceilings, not padded row counts. Bands8/4/2/1 regroup
  surviving eligible rows after EOS/length/cancellation. Real prelaunch
  admission None can lower a band; other errors propagate to original owners.
- B6 initially hit CUDA OOM after completed old-stream memory pools accumulated
  across models. Cold cleanup now runs under original initialization/queue
  guards. Actual repetition freed completed idle pools; no unsafe reset/recovery.
- B7 per-row positions drive RoPE, KV append, causal softmax and AV. Mixed
  positions255/256/0/31/32/1/510/511, refill and feedback compare fullV/all42.
  Padded AV must skip inactive FMA lanes; canonical future zeros remain exact.
- B8 partitions StateOnly prefix work from final prompt-tail greedy work before
  banding. Every teacher advances its own state/cursor but emits no generated
  ID/Text/usage/Done. EOS **as a teacher** is ordinary input. Ragged tails may
  finish through B1; prefix HTTP tests must not demand unrelated greedy fusion.
- Current native scheduler consumes one teacher per row/wave, including unmatched
  B1 native-mode rows. Interleaved retains max32 prefix quantum. This exposes
  host/root/readback overhead and motivates the paused temporal proposals.

## 6. Benchmark/profiler lifecycle lessons and known failures

  whole-group cleanup and00d1 record-only TERM+INT guard. Preserve these exact
  seams when copying helpers; comments about finite cleanup are not proof.

  Guard records a flag; explicit checkpoints raise only after ownership exists.
  Original drain is restored before retirement; failure/receipt/log errors
  prevent the next provider. Every nonzero group signal precedes first reap.
- Podman cleanup authenticates nonce/name/CID, retries bounded stop/force removal,
  reaps original foreground/group and rediscovers owned startup races. Unknown
  HPIDs establish no ownership; GPU membership must match numeric owned PIDs.

  `podman unshare → unshare --net --mount → root-private-loopback-exec-2.py`.

- Initial FlashInfer read-only `/root/.cache` failure was fixed through the
  public pinned FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BASE=/tmp setting for both arms, not HOME
  replacement or a model math change. Initial GPU membership failures were
  diagnosed by bounded raw evidence, not relaxed ownership predicates.
- Actual vLLM module/dist version and Podman image bareId versus sha256 prefix

## 11. Independent performance investigation — durable prose copy

The following report was prepared under investigation/planning-only authority.
It consolidates measured bottlenecks versus hypotheses, shared-engine priorities,
benchmark matrix/tool gaps and27B capacity. It is reproduced here so its prose
survives eventual ignored-run cleanup. Original location:
`.agents/runs/serving-and-speculation-performance-audit-batch-20261020/REPORT.md`.

### Shared-engine performance audit — planning only

Owner: batch_design_review. Parent: serving-and-speculation; ROOT consolidates.
No code, tests, builds, model/provider/GPU/container execution or payload scans.
This is an independent recommendation, not a new implementation tracker.

#### Conclusion

The strongest immediate target is the repeated single-teacher execution path,
not a larger advertised batch flag. Native multi-request B2/4/8 is real, but
prefill still advances one teacher per request/wave and emits thousands of
kernels per model-token. A credible route toward vLLM performance combines
temporal prefill, exact leaf fusion, substantially better projection kernels
and eventually production-safe graph replay. None alone establishes a win.

Numerical correctness and physical ownership are release gates for every cut.
The current GGUF CPU-target profile and stock's loaded BF16 arithmetic are
different targets. Faster execution of one does not establish cross-engine
equivalence; the common GPU profile remains a critical-path requirement.

#### What is measured, and what is inferred

| 2B canonical IDs/usage/text match on one prompt, seven-prompt quality still unqualified | V8 policy/quality/pre-benchmark records | Matching one greedy response does not qualify hidden states or numerical profile. .8B canonical responses differ. |
| Warmed native C1 TTFT about4.09s/.8B and4.72s/2B |32-process native-only A/B | Cold/warm gap makes lazy compilation/allocation/initialization a necessary diagnostic. Different experiments; do not subtract them as a measured JIT duration. |
| Native prefix batching cuts earlier concurrent source launches about82%, improving finite-wave time43%/.8B and33%/2B | Native-prefix warm observations | Multi-request prefix fusion matters; C1 changes little. All concurrent samples still miss10s TTFT. |

| 64328 actual native kernels in short B2 window; SiLU15.67%, finite14.27%, merge8.13%, copies5.76% of count | Validated native CUPTI +small family histogram | Real count inventory, **not latency fractions** and not canonical C1/current candidate. |

TensorCore/CMMA use is absent from these paths. Compute/BW/occupancy dominance is not measured. |

#### Priorities and measurable gates

##### 0. Close the comparable numerical target and benchmark accounting

- Keep native GGUF regression optimization against accepted independent CPU/B1
  full-vocabulary/all42 references. Keep original-HF official loader, restored
  F32 CPU profile and stock CUDA loaded-cast profile explicitly distinct.

  casts, BF16 projection reductions, GDN/FLA initial versus cached schedule,

  public GemmEx settings are useful antecedents, not full-model equivalence.

  validated parity record and original physical publication/committed-token

  profile, graph/program generation, generation policy, source/test scope and

comparison rejects stale/incompatible parity records and unverifiable commits.
No source-correct performance claim until these prerequisites hold.

##### 1. Obtain a critical-path decomposition before choosing further kernels

Use separate diagnostic processes/windows, never profiled main timing samples.
Derive kernel-duration totals and interval unions, launch/API blocking time,
host gaps, H2D/D2H and device-copy bytes, synchronization count, allocation,
compile/cache misses and shape reuse. Sum of overlapping durations is not wall
time. Associate data with prefill/decode/maintenance and exact request/window.

- Compare cold-process versus declared warm conditions; explicitly attribute
  compile, initialization and H2D rather than moving cost behind readiness and
  claiming it disappeared. Report startup-to-ready separately.
- Close native/stock collector coverage, losses, child-process/PID attribution
  and device/RAM overhead. Native counter equality applies only to its exact
  workload; graph enqueue1 is not underlying kernel count1.
- Establish a simple roofline for projection/state traffic from **measured**
  bytes and time. Counts, low point GPU utilization and code inspection alone
  cannot distinguish bandwidth, arithmetic, launch bubbles or host stalls.

Acceptance: diagnostic output transparency, zero lost/unowned activity and
closed owners; explain the dominant measured latency components before a major
kernel rewrite. Existing bounded trace may support offline analysis by ROOT;
this investigation did not scan its raw payload.

##### 3. Temporal prefill, including the dominant solo case

Two distinct milestones must not be conflated:

1. Sequential T2/T4 state-only chunk: gather once, existing B-body repeatedT,

them in that dependency order, including solo B1; optimizing only C8 cannot fix
the observed C1 gap. Do not label a B-loop or sequentialT loop native temporal

- First exact GGUF route: tile output/request rows, coalesce packed weight loads,

  Investigate DP4A or bounded integer MMA only when integer subresults can match
  original lane/block grouping and overflow limits exactly. Do not reassociate
  FP scale reductions, replace activation quantization or narrow precision.
- Precompute immutable source scale metadata only under the source identity and
  physical budget; avoid persistent expanded weights exceeding admission.
- Separate common-HF CUDA route: native BF16 tiled/TensorCore projection in the
  SAME operator/provider seam is essential research for vLLM-class arithmetic
  intensity. Public GemmEx settings do not identify its hidden reduction kernel.
  Original-actor stream/handle/workspace/internal allocation/Ready ownership and
  authentic operand parity must close before a cuBLAS provider is admitted.
- Existing exact CPU-target BF16 CUDA kernel intentionally reproduces CPU64
  order and is not evidence of stock CUDA arithmetic or TensorCore throughput.

Acceptance: operator timing, achieved BW/occupancy/reuse, all codec scale/code/
intermediate/status bits, source-independent adversaries, complete model/state
and resource safety. TensorCore math requires its declared independently proven
GPU profile; it is not a universal replacement for CPU-exact GGUF reductions.

##### 5. Production graph reuse and synchronization reduction

Private graph proof exists; production admission does not. Close participation
for every same-card command, constructor/init H2D/allocation, external event/
storage, sync and final Drop. Same original actor/stream and fair queue only;
no second context, global mutex held across await or caller isolation fiction.

- Capture fixed owned math workspace; dynamic original-root gather/candidate
  scatter and independent publication stay outside. Keys bind source/program
  generation, numerical profile, row band/capacity/readout and relevant shapes.
- Bound graph/executable/driver metadata, cache entries and retirement owners.
  Eviction waits for real completion; unknown completion quarantines owners.
- Device-token feedback and graph variants need their own proof; current private
  host-teacher proof does not authorize them. Cold admission refusal can choose
  another qualified path; post-launch errors cannot become fallback.

Acceptance: physical exclusivity under competing init/Drop/commands, fairness,
epoch revocation, no capture allocation leaks, CPU/B1/native all42/fullV,
abort/pressure/cache invalidation and final0. Measure host enqueue/bubbles/TTFT;
underlying kernels remainK per replay even when host graph API calls become1.

##### 6. State traffic, attention and scheduling capacity

- Measure bytes first: current packed gather/scatter remains real state traffic
  even after row transport cut its kernel count. Consider direct per-row leased
  state bindings for uncaptured kernels, or immutable paged KV/prefix sharing
  under the original source/session lineage and physical ownership. GDN private
  candidate state still needs genuine independent writes. Do not alias writable
  roots or infer unpublished candidates are safe to overwrite.
- Graph fixed buffers and direct dynamic state bindings have different ownership
  constraints; benchmark both after qualification instead of silently capturing
  mutable published-state pointers.
- Fused attention/softmax and more parallel GDN/chunk prefill can be major long
  context work. FlashAttention/FLA cannot simply replace the CPU-target schedule:
  casts, reductions, masking, padded lanes and initial/cached order need their
  own independently verified common GPU contract.
- Continue ragged band/refill/age-aware decode-prefill scheduling; retain real
  typed capacity refusal and2/4/8→smaller bands, output credits, at-most-once SSE
  and prompt/decode fairness. Measure offered load and aging, not just full waves.
  Raise concurrency/geometry only after actual active-state/metadata/graph/cache
  admission; no silent bump to fill the GPU.

#### Fair staged benchmark matrix

Use unchanged canonical serve-bench.py/serve-compare.py and a new explicit
protocol derivative when metrics/parity hooks are added. Existing compare caps:
requests<=128, concurrency1..8, repetitions1..4; bench has other bounds, which
do not authorize changing compare/admission. Start at C1/2/4/8. Keep all failures.

| Stage | Work | Conditions / purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A: exact regression | Existing47-ID prompt/max8 plus seven-prompt quality, genuine EOS and unequal outputs | .8B/2B, complete state/logits first; preserve current comparability/history. |
| B: startup/solo | Canonical C1 cold-process and warm-process | First after readiness versus exactly one canonical ordinary warmup. Separately report process startup-to-ready. Neither means storage-cold. |
| C: concurrent | Canonical C2/4/8 finite waves, then bounded repeated waves | Test true fusion, shape/JIT warm effects and tail retirement; ordinary C1 warmup does not fully warm C8. Add an explicitly separate shape-warmed protocol if desired, symmetrically for both. |
| D: prefill/decode shape | Short1/32/47 input, medium128 input, long448 input; outputs8/64 where capacity fits | Current accepted GPU capacity512 constrains prompt+actual generated frontier. Do not schedule512+64 or advertise8K GPU serving. Report actual IDs/EOS-dependent work. |
| E: interference/SLO | Open-loop fixed arrivals, long-prefill plus short decode, ragged refills, cancellation/backpressure and two workload labels | Sweep offered rates through saturation, finite queue and fixed deadline; test starvation, overload and committed goodput, not a closed-loop throughput illusion. Labels are not authenticated tenant isolation. |
| F: best route | Genuine pinned stock default/graphs versus qualified ZG best path | Eager/eager is a diagnostic row. Do not handicap stock to eager and call it best vLLM, or enable private ZG graphs prematurely. |

Keep equivalent weights/quantization/loaded casts/tokenizer/template/generation,
actual raw token IDs, EOS/usage/finish, source/hardware/context and policy limits.
Use the same original rootless/private isolation, GPU UUID, CPU4/12GiB RAM/swap0
and declared device envelope as current .8B/2B protocol; collect actual readbacks.
Changing caps or admission is a new point for BOTH providers, not a rescue run.
Counterbalanced ABBA/BAAB fresh-process blocks remain useful. More evidence can
use repeated bounded outer blocks without silently raising tool limits.

Report offered/accepted/rejected/timed-out/cancelled/completed requests, committed
and delivered tokens, p50/p95/p99 TTFT and **actual individual-token** ITL,
SLO-qualified committed goodput per offered second, queue/client backlog,
memory allocation peaks versus point samples, power/clocks/temperature, fairness
and actual hardware kernels/direct APIs/graph enqueues separately. Coalesced IDs
leave per-token delivery unresolved; mean ITL or SSE chunk timing cannot repair it.

Add paired process/block confidence intervals for predeclared primary metrics.
Do not treat tokens within one process as independent repetitions or median
per-sample p95 as a pooled p95. Check thermal/order effects and all losing points.
A speed claim needs a confidence-supported improvement on its named workload
with source-correct SLO-goodput and predeclared latency/resource/no-starvation
constraints. A finite-wave win is not sustained capacity or broad vLLM parity.

#### Model feasibility and dependencies

| Model | Honest next scope | Main blockers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3.5 .8B | Accepted GGUF exact serving optimization and common-HF GPU qualification; bounded matched C1/2/4/8 after parity | Current cross-profile quality/state gap; token-major prefill, scalar projection path, production graphs/stock collector closure. |
| Qwen3.5 2B | Same engine/cuts, actual2B per-shape/resource proof rather than .8B extrapolation | HF shard4.548GB exceeds old4GiB complete-source guard; differing original/loaded casts, initial/attention/FLA closure; tighter active/workspace capacity. |
| Original Qwen3.8 27B | Finish initial exp/provider/core +common typed full model/112-domain CPU truth, then source-window streamed CPU/GPU and matched feasible offload | Isolated wide/cached/gamma operators pass but full model absent. Full55.563GB source cannot reside in current12GiB process cap or6GiB GPU. No stock exact-architecture/offload equivalence is established. |

Actual retained hardware is an RTX3060 **Laptop6GiB**, not a12GiB desktop card.
Current GPU operator envelope5GiB/provider4GiB is smaller again. Nominal27B
2-bit weights alone are about6.75GB before block metadata/state/workspace, so
even that is not an assumed fully resident solution. No such qualified source
is implied by a metadata listing. BF16 needs streamed/offloaded windows or a
separately authorized larger hardware configuration.

For27B, first prove the same engine's full original math and state; then measure
SSD/RAM/GPU bytes, throughput, source leases, I/O completion and overlap with
actual ResourceArbiter readiness. Multi-teacher prefill can amortize each staged
weight tile; streaming decode must disclose bandwidth/cache limits. Compare only
against stock's genuinely supported same source/profile/offload policy and caps.
If stock or ZG cannot execute that point, mark it infeasible/unqualified rather
than substitute another model/quantization/device or invent a benchmark.
````

````markdown
# Correctness first, then measured vLLM performance

Author: pvl
Co-authors: Codex, baseline_review, spine_review, batch_design_review
Owner: @pvl
Date: 2026-10-20
Source checkpoint: `fb68d8fa165de16e21d1bd37afef3790b80da971`
Status: investigation and proposed implementation plan only; implementation paused.

## 1. Decision and scope

First make Qwen3.5-0.8B, Qwen3.5-2B and original Qwen3.8-27B numerically
correct under explicit reference arithmetic. Then optimize the same engine
and demonstrate a workload-specific advantage over pinned vLLM.

Use pinned vLLM as the primary target for the new CUDA execution profile.
Treat it as correct unless an independent counterexample establishes otherwise.
Keep the accepted llama.cpp reference and Torch CPU profiles as regression
oracles. Their differing reductions and casts must not be silently combined
into an invented fourth reference.

This document records the implementation sequence and acceptance decisions.
The existing [numerics TODO](TODO.md), [model execution TODO](../model-execution/TODO.md)
and [serving TODO](../serving-and-speculation/TODO.md) remain the only owning
queues. No implementation or numerical gate is completed by writing this plan.

**Fastest route:** reproduce the earliest differing operation with identical
inputs; port its actual reference arithmetic; immediately compose its real
producer and consumer; progress to a complete layer and model. Avoid extended
standalone helper work that never reaches a real token.

## 2. What the evidence establishes

| Area | Established | Still missing |
|---|---|---|
| Small-model GGUF reference profile | Fresh mixed/Unicode corpus through 8K; both models match pinned llama.cpp AR1 and explicit `use_ref` control at the recorded checkpoints: 730 selected records, full 248,320 logits, all 42 causal domains; 55,382,016 state words/model at 8K | Default bulk arithmetic and the unrecovered historical corpus |
| Native small-model CUDA | Complete B=2/4/8 model graphs, independent row positions, CPU/B1 logits and all 42 domains within accepted source/context scope | Broader independent numeric profiles, genuine long-context GPU, temporal prefill |
| Original HF CPU | Numerous source-bound operators and isolated compositions pass; original reference captures exist | Complete trained .8B/2B/27B model composition and full-state/logit parity |
| Original 27B | Original source acquired; H48 cached recurrence, gated norm and wide-role isolated tests pass | Live producers, complete initial chunk, complete model/112 domains, admitted physical execution |
| vLLM | Genuine pinned V1 and official GGUF plugin ran both small models | Cross-engine full numerical/state parity, optimized default-route warm/concurrent comparison |
| Performance | Bounded eager C1 comparison shows a large native deficit | Numerical qualification of compared profiles and representative performance advantage |

The original assertion that complete B>1 GPU fusion is absent is superseded
by accepted P12-B7 and later work. Cross-request full-model fusion exists.
Temporal prefill still executes a full model step per prompt token.

No evidence currently proves a single defective GDN recurrence equation is
the cause of every discrepancy. “First difference observed in GDN” is not
equivalent to “GDN produced the first numerical error.”

## 3. Divergence inventory and fixes

“Proven difference” below means the cited source or executed comparison
establishes that difference. It does not automatically establish a defect in
a separately declared arithmetic profile. This is the complete currently
identified inventory, not a claim that undiscovered bugs cannot remain.

Select that contract only for the matching bulk profile. Then rerun layer3→layer4 and the complete prefix. |

## 4. Numerical contracts

### 4.1 Keep four targets explicit

| Target | Purpose | Required identity |
|---|---|---|
| Accepted GGUF AR1/reference | Preserve working CPU/CUDA behavior and independently exact fresh8K results | Original GGUF, existing reduction/quant policy, F32 KV, FA off in reference |
| Pinned llama.cpp default bulk | Explain and reproduce the default comparison discrepancy | `d812350`, actual CPU/BLAS route, batch/ubatch, strides, thread count, temporary quant format |
| Pinned Torch CPU original HF | Independent trained-source oracle and existing CPU operator work | Effective loaded tensor dtypes, Torch/provider versions, vector width/tails, initial/cached schedule |
| Pinned vLLM CUDA | Primary new correctness and performance target | vLLM, plugin, source/loader, CUDA kernels, phase, activation/state dtype, compiler/math modes |

Extend `ProgramNumericalProfile` and typed operator contracts in the existing
core; the proposed vLLM and bulk profiles do not exist in MAIN today.
Profile identity belongs in compiled-plan/cache keys and state compatibility.
Reject incompatible reuse rather than choosing a dtype from a display name.

### 4.2 Mathematical GDN definition

For each value head, let `S[k,v]` be its FP32 recurrent matrix, with independent
convolution history and causal frontier. Original 27B uses 128 key/value
dimensions and repeats each of 16 Q/K heads into three adjacent value heads.
Converted GGUF layouts require their own verified mapping.
This mathematical notation is the transpose of vLLM's actual contiguous-key
`[head,value,key]` cache; it is not permission to reinterpret the bytes.

The semantic recurrence is:

```text
u_t = depthwise_conv4(project_qkv(x_t), prior_history)
(q_t, k_t, v_t) = split(SiLU(u_t))
qhat = q_t / sqrt(sum(q_t*q_t) + eps_l2)
khat = k_t / sqrt(sum(k_t*k_t) + eps_l2)
qscaled = qhat / sqrt(key_dim)
beta = sigmoid(project_b(x_t))
g = -exp(A_log) * softplus(project_a(x_t) + dt_bias)
d = exp(g)
Sdecayed[k,v] = d * Sprevious[k,v]
prediction[v] = sum_k(khat[k] * Sdecayed[k,v])
delta[v] = beta * (v_t[v] - prediction[v])
Snext[k,v] = Sdecayed[k,v] + khat[k] * delta[v]
core[v] = sum_k(qscaled[k] * Snext[k,v])
gated = RMS(core, eps_norm) * gamma * SiLU(project_z(x_t))
output = project_out(gated)
```

These equations specify algebra, not floating-point instruction order.
For the pinned target, the required implementation also includes each cast,
reduction tree, FMA boundary, exponential approximation and layout.
Pinned vLLM Q/K L2 epsilon is fixed `1e-6`; gated RMS uses
`config.rms_norm_eps`. These are separate fields.
Do not reuse GGUF grouped-RMS lowering as proof of the original FLA algorithm.

### 4.3 Exactness rules

- BF16 stores: round-to-nearest, ties-to-even at the reference boundary;
  preserve signed zero. Widening BF16 to F32 is exact and is not an extra
  rounding step.
- Raw learned parameters retain their actual dtype and source role. Ordinary
  Qwen RMS's `1 + weight` semantics do not apply to GDN's raw learned gamma.
- FP32 state remains FP32; BF16 core/output does not permit BF16 recurrent
  storage. Preserve source accumulation order and every materialized boundary.
- Source FMA is one rounding; separate multiply/add is two. Do not enable
  blanket fast-math or silently contract a CPU tensor expression.
- Padding is masked according to the reference. An intentional `-Inf`
  triangular mask is valid only inside that closed operator; it does not
  weaken general finite-value validation. Do not multiply poisoned future
  values by zero and assume the result is harmless.
- Pin denormal/FTZ behavior, exponential/reciprocal implementation, matrix
  compute/output types and TF32 settings. A cuBLAS API's “FP32 accumulation”
  does not reveal its reduction tree.
- Kernel source alone cannot establish the exact generated CUDA instruction
  stream. Where bit identity is promised, replay actual compiled kernels on
  authentic operands. Record unresolved instruction/provider details as
  unresolved rather than filling them in from algebra.

### 4.4 Initial prefill versus decode

Use the actual selected pinned vLLM kernel, not a kernel guessed from an
environment-variable name. On SM86 the inspected automatic prefill branch
selects Triton. With packed decode enabled, ordinary non-speculative decode
selects `_forward_core_decode_non_spec` and Triton packed recurrence.
`GDN_DECODE_KERNEL=cuda` alone does not prove the guarded C++ MTP path ran.
Confirm branch/environment at runtime when implementation resumes.

**Normal packed decode, all temporaries F32:** widen conv output; divide Q/K
by `sqrt(sum(square)+1e-6)`; multiply Q by `K**-0.5` before readout; compute
`x=a+dt_bias`, `softplus=select(x<=20,log(1+exp(x)),x)`,
`g=-exp(A_log)*softplus`, `beta=sigmoid(b)`; decay state, subtract its K dot
from V, multiply residual by beta, update state and reduce against scaled Q.
Store core BF16 and recurrent state in its explicitly configured FP32 cache.
The state-decay exp alias is `tl.exp` by default and `fast_expf` under
`FLA_USE_FAST_OPS=1`; coefficient exp/log/sigmoid are direct Triton operations.
Preserve the selected setting and validate generated arithmetic.

**CUDA initial/continued prefill, chunk64:**

1. Conv FP32 accumulation → `acc/(1+exp(-acc))` → BF16 store.
   Normalize Q/K in F32 using reciprocal sqrt, multiply, then store BF16.
   V remains BF16; beta and log-gates are F32.
2. Prefill softplus uses the stable positive branch
   `x+log(1+exp(-x))`, nonpositive `log(1+exp(x))`, then threshold20.
   This differs from the decode expression; do not collapse the two.
3. Compute chunk-local F32 prefix log-gates `G=cumsum(g)`.
   Form the strict-lower system
   `A[i,j]=dot(beta[i]*k[i],k[j])*exp(G[i]-G[j])` in the source graph.
   Beta multiplies the operand before the dot; moving it outside changes
   rounding. Keep the promoted operand dtype selected by the CUDA branch.
4. `solve_tril` forms `(I+A)^-1`, including its source negation and unit
   diagonal. Preserve the 16×16 solve and block-merge order rather than
   substituting a generic inverse. It returns **BF16 K dtype**.
   Pin `FLA_TRIL_PRECISION` (source default `ieee`) and actual dot policies.
   The WY construction casts scaled V/K operands to BF16 before its dots;
   `u` and `w` outputs are BF16.
5. Running state stays F32 `[head,value,key]`; each chunk's saved entering
   state `h` is BF16. Compute `v_new=u-w@h` and store BF16. Apply chunk decay
   to F32 state; cast the decay-adjusted delta BF16 before its K/delta dot.
   Final recurrent state is F32.
6. Output uses BF16 Q/K/h/v_new dots with F32 accumulators and causal masks;
   gate-adjusted attention coefficients are cast BF16 before the V dot.
   Scale both output terms, add and store BF16.
7. Gated RMS widens the BF16 core, computes norm/gamma/SiLU product in F32,
   then stores once to BF16. No CPU intermediate BF16 gamma-product cast.

This is a mixed-precision chunk/WY algorithm. Keep sequential recurrence as
an independent semantic oracle; it is not an instruction-exact substitute.
Reproduce actual reductions, masks and boundary state from the pinned kernels.
No newly executed vLLM→Rust operator comparison is asserted by this table.

The existing Torch CPU target has a distinct known schedule:

1. Widen and normalize Q/K; initial query multiplies F32 `0x3db504f3`.
   Cached query divides by rounded F32 sqrt(128).
2. Initial short input pads to64; materialize beta*K and beta*V.
3. Prefix scan uses F64 carry with an F32 store at each element.
4. Form masked prefix differences, exponentials, Gram products and
   unit-lower solves; retain materialized intermediate boundaries.
5. Preserve the six recorded BMM families and two solve groups, column-major
   solve outputs and final valid-row extraction. State remains FP32.
6. Cached update uses materialized products/reductions, separate subtraction,
   multiplication and addition. Its tested state uses key-major orientation.

This CPU schedule must not be copied into vLLM's Triton path merely because
both implement GDN. Conversely, vLLM's fused casts must not replace the
already qualified CPU profile.

### 4.5 Small-model default bulk arithmetic

The minimal existing candidate implements one eight-lane FP32 FMA accumulator
per output, processing K in eight-element groups, including the source's
zero-filled tail operations. Its horizontal sum follows the pinned low/high
lane additions, then `(low0 + low2) + (low1 + low3)`. AR1's four partial
accumulators remain a separate contract.

Validate the original strided AV and F32 alpha captures, together covering
132,096 output words. Then advance through downstream routes, including
Q8/dequant/BLAS. The prepared `root-default-bulk-20261020` worktree is
uncompiled and unqualified; its existence is not a fix.

## 5. Porting strategy and implementation boundaries

Port small mathematical operations and the reference's phase/layout logic.
Reuse the existing `MathematicalBackend`, `ForwardPlan`, source descriptors,
`HostMath`, resident GPU queue, `ResourceArbiter` and `SessionAuthority`.

| Existing area | Intended change after implementation resumes |
|---|---|
| `zerogravity-core/src/accelerator/program/typed.rs` and typed children | Explicit profile, phase, dtype and layout contracts; only qualified operations become selectable |
| `zerogravity-cpu/src/original_hf/` and `src/math/` | Independent semantic/source-profile reference operations; preserve accepted CPU schedules |
| `zerogravity-model-qwen35/src/forward.rs`, `host_math/`, source bindings | Compose actual trained producers in the existing plan; preserve source-derived geometry and state effects |
| `zerogravity-gpu/src/resident_program.rs` and operator modules | vLLM-profile CUDA operations and temporal kernels through the original queue |
| `resident_inference.rs`, `resident_batch.rs` | Phase-aware temporal prefill, independent rows, state/currentness and physical completion |
| `zerogravity/src/original_qwen_math.rs` | Keep diagnostic labeling explicit; do not promote it to a second production engine |

Do not port vLLM's Python model/session engine or allocator. If a provider
kernel is reused directly, it must fit the original physical admission,
buffer lifetime, event and quarantine model. A Python subprocess is an
independent oracle, not a production inference fallback.

Preserve upstream license/SPDX notices and exact source revision when porting.
Prefer the actual selected upstream kernel over a convenient unused helper.
No new broad plugin framework is needed for a handful of typed operations.

## 6. Fast implementation sequence, when resumed

### C0 — Lock the comparison, not another framework

Use existing raw teacher IDs, retained captures and pinned runtimes.
For each run record the model/source, effective loaded dtypes, phase,
chunk size, state layout and operation route in the existing test output.
Reuse existing process ownership and reference tools.

Choose the lane explicitly. Recommended primary lane: original .8B HF with
vLLM's actual loaded GPU dtypes, avoiding the extra GGUF log/exp and temporary
quantization transformations during the first GDN diagnosis. Use that same
profile for 2B/27B when admitted. Keep the existing GGUF-plugin benchmark lane
separate; it must reproduce its own loader/quantizer to qualify numerically.
Neither lane's pure operator captures may be relabeled as the other's.

For .8B, begin with teachers11/353 and the first64 corpus. Capture projected
QKV/Z/a/b before GDN to determine whether a projection mismatch already
precedes the known cast differences. Do not assume the diagnostic matches
vLLM at its GDN inputs.
Bind actual phase and partition metadata: teacher353 must really take the
claimed cached/continued route. Repeat the exact reference partition in each
comparison; different chunkings or GEMM shapes are not automatically bit-equal
because they share a profile name.

Exit: the first differing operation has identical compared inputs and source
weights, or the earlier source/loader/projection mismatch is precisely located.

### C1 — Close the earliest small-model default discrepancies

Compile and test the existing bulk primitive; replay AV and alpha.
Compose real producer→operator→consumer and run the same first64 tokens.
Follow the next actual difference, including beta and Q8/BLAS output routes.

Keep this a bounded CPU side task while the vLLM CUDA profile is developed.
Do not delay the primary vLLM route on recovering an unavailable historical
file or on completing an unrelated generic arithmetic framework.

Exit: exact authentic leaf replays and a declared complete default schedule
comparison; accepted AR1 results unchanged. Historical closure remains
separate if its raw inputs cannot be recovered.

### C2 — Complete one vLLM-profile GDN layer

After projection parity, implement convolution+SiLU → phase-specific Q/K
normalization/replication → coefficients. Qualify the smaller cached core
and gated RMS first using authentic nonzero prior state, then implement
initial/continued-prefill chunk64 and connect initial→cached continuation
plus output projection. Start with .8B, then use 2B and H48/27B for geometry.
Completing the separate Torch CPU MKL/BLAS provider is not a prerequisite
for the vLLM CUDA port.

For every fix require a failing-before/passing-after genuine-operand case.
Compare full intermediates and state, not just one output element.
Connect each accepted operation immediately; imported reference operands may
isolate a bug but cannot replace the native producer in the composed gate.

Exit: initial layer output/state followed by genuine cached continuation
matches the target; no reference intermediate is injected into the final test.

### C3 — Complete .8B, then 2B in the same plan

Compose all layers: embedding, norms, full attention, GDN, residuals, MLP,
final norm and head. Trace the first new mismatch rather than repeatedly
dumping every later error. Inspect the full 248,320 logits and all42 domains.

First B1, then B2/4/8, ragged positions, refill and B1↔batch transitions.
Do not carry an assumption that one-token and bulk GEMM use identical
reductions; qualify the actual selected algorithms/shapes.
The source-correct safe chunk path is itself part of correctness; its initial
implementation need not yet be the fastest temporal-prefill implementation.

Exit: small-model full correctness matrix below, including initial→decode
and whole-prefill→chunked-prefill continuations.

### C4 — Complete original27B without relaxing resource guards

Use the same recipe/operations with source-derived geometry: 64 layers,
48 GDN/16 full-attention layers, 112 state domains, hidden5120,
MLP17408, vocabulary248320 and an untied head.

Reuse verified source windows and isolated H48/wide-role work, including the
already tested full17408-column CPU down-projection role. Finish live
coefficients, initial chunk and trained producer/full-model composition.
The corresponding native GPU wide-column path remains unqualified;
geometry refusal must not be removed without the corresponding arithmetic.

Original BF16 weights are about55.56GB. They cannot fit the local6GiB GPU;
current executable-source and GPU-width guards also remain. First establish
complete CPU/reference execution on an admitted capable host or correctly
accounted source-window path. For GPU serving choose either a capable
matched resident device or complete physical RAM/SSD/GPU streaming.
Compare vLLM under the same capacity/offload constraints; an unsupported
comparison is reported as unavailable.

Exit: original27B full logits/all112 domains and continuation qualify.
Operator-only success, acquired metadata and a source window are not this gate.

### C5 — Accept and checkpoint

Run focused regressions, relevant strict Clippy, physical CUDA/state/cancel
tests, both approved original cache-direct/HF-import release routes and:

```sh
CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 RAYON_NUM_THREADS=4 python3 scripts/native-gpu.py -- bash scripts/check.sh
```

Use one MAIN Cargo/GPU coordinator; independent agents own disjoint source
cuts/reviews. Preserve root README, unrelated overlays and the Renoir/gfx90c
launch hold. Review and sign only owned verified changes. Reconcile existing
plan TODOs; no extra status ledger or source-inventory framework.

## 7. Numerical parity matrix and acceptance

| Axis | Small first gate | Expansion required for the claim |
|---|---|---|
| Sources | .8B original GGUF and official HF, explicitly separate | 2B equivalents; original27B, then individually qualified quant profiles |
| Teacher inputs | Tokens11/353; retained mixed/Unicode first64 | Fixed raw IDs for prose, code, Unicode, repeats, zeros/extreme operator inputs; held-out prompts |
| Phase boundaries | Empty→first prefill→cached step | 1/2/31/32/63/64/65/127/128/129 tokens; ragged chunks and continued prefill |
| Context | Short complete model | 512/1024/2048/4096/8192; 16K/32K only after actual capacity and predecessor gates |
| Batch | B1 | B2/4/8, independent positions, refill, row reorder, canceled neighbor |
| Outputs | Full affected tensor/state | Every layer residual, full248320 logits, all42 or112 domains and next-token continuation |
| State lifecycle | Initial and cached | Snapshot/restore, fork/COW, cancellation before/after submission, failure/quarantine, final reclaim |

Required distinguishing tests, using independently generated expected values:

- Conv sums straddling a BF16 rounding boundary before SiLU; one-store CUDA
  and two-store CPU results must remain distinguishable.
- Nonzero beta that changes under premature BF16 rounding; positive/negative
  softplus inputs and values on either side of20, separately for both phases.
- Zero/tiny/nontrivial Q/K sums; prefill BF16 versus cached F32 normalized
  vectors and fixed L2 epsilon independent of model norm epsilon.
- Asymmetric `HK=2,HV=6` sentinels proving `[0,0,0,1,1,1]` grouping; genuine
  16→48 source/canonical permutation and quantized output-layout checks.
- Nonuniform signed prior state and Q exposing transpose and scale-before/
  scale-after reduction; a zero-state-only fixture would miss both.
- F32 and BF16 raw gamma cases distinguishing promotion from intermediate
  BF16 rounding; compare the relevant CPU and CUDA targets separately.
- Length63/64/65 with nonzero initial state and invalid padded lanes;
  compare solved-A, u/w, saved h, v_new, final state and complete next output.

Three separate verdicts are required:

1. **Same source and same arithmetic contract:** exact bits for promised
   leaf replays, deterministic internal CPU/B1/batch state/logits and integer
   layouts. Zero-sign differences are reported, not silently normalized.
   Phase, shape, partition and selected kernel are part of that contract;
   cross-partition algorithm changes use a separately qualified comparison.
2. **Independent implementations with deliberately different arithmetic:**
   report max absolute/relative error, RMS/relative-L2, ULP distribution,
   full-vocabulary distribution metrics, top-k/rank and per-domain drift.
   Preserve existing numerical limits: historical functional shared-top20
   logprob0.45 and top-token probability0.05 are only those specific tests,
   not permission for arbitrary state error or a new universal tolerance.
3. **Model behavior:** teacher-forced loss/perplexity, continuation and task
   quality on held-out checkpoint-matched inputs; stochastic policy and
   sampling distribution separately when advertised.

There is no existing universal BF16 state/logit tolerance that can honestly
be asserted to qualify all three models against every vLLM kernel.
For a newly different arithmetic route, define its per-operator/state/error
budget from the pinned reference and sensitivity study **before evaluating
the candidate for promotion**; record it in the existing numerical contract.
Until that budget exists and passes, it is unqualified. Do not choose bounds
after seeing the candidate error or relabel a failed exact test as approximate.

For the fastest initial implementation, retain the target's own casts and
operation order and aim for exact genuine-operand replays. This minimizes
the need to justify new approximation budgets. A cuBLAS reduction difference
must still be investigated rather than hidden by the high-level equations.

## 8. Why performance is currently far behind

The actual eager first-request-after-readiness comparison measured median
TTFT13.400s versus1.561s for .8B and14.540s versus1.562s for2B.
The2B individual-token delivery p95 was approximately0.186–0.199s native
versus0.026–0.030s stock. This is a real observed deficit in that bounded
configuration, not evidence of numerical equivalence or every workload.
Separate native warm experiments show substantially lower C1 latency.
Their difference from the cold experiment is not a measured JIT duration:
profile lazy compilation, initialization and allocations explicitly.

Concrete causes/limitations to address:

- `resident_inference.rs` still iterates prompt tokens and awaits a complete
  model execution for each. Cross-request batching does not supply a
  token-matrix prefill or a chunk-parallel GDN algorithm.
- The canonical .8B C1 window launched236,270 native kernels for54 model
  steps. Native launch coverage was verified. Stock recorded9,318 kernel
  activities, but complete/lossless stock coverage was not established;
  do not claim an exact hardware-count ratio.
- Source launch attribution includes41,148 SiLU launches,58,144
  certification/merge launches and20,768 RMS launches. These are launch
  counts, not measured percentages of runtime.
- The latest accepted C8 change cut source dispatch counts by about18% but
  improved observed median raw token rates only about1.7%; C1 barely changed.
  Fewer launches alone are a poor predictor of the remaining speedup.
- Both compared routes were eager. Missing native production CUDA graphs
  cannot explain this particular eager-versus-eager deficit by itself.
- Tiny step projections, reduction kernels, synchronization, allocations and
  state movement are likely important; rank them by actual stage/device
  timing and bytes, not by kernel count alone.

There is no basis for saying all vLLM optimizations are already implemented.
Existing source/state safety and fusion foundations do not guarantee faster
execution. Correctness and a Rust host implementation alone imply no speedup.

## 9. Performance sequence after correctness

The order below targets structural work before local tuning. A bounded,
already-prepared fusion can land earlier if it proves a useful gain without
delaying the correctness or temporal-prefill path.
If measured host gaps dominate, graph admission may proceed alongside
projection work; the priorities are evidence-driven, not a fixed calendar.

| Priority | Change in shared machinery | Why / measurement | Required guard |
|---|---|---|---|
| P0 | Establish accepted numeric-profile baseline, phase timing, device events, bytes, CPU submission gaps and physical counts | Identify prefill/decode bottlenecks and separate GPU work from launch/host waits | Unprofiled paired timings remain the performance result; instrumented outputs match plain outputs |
| P1 | True temporal prefill: token-matrix projections/MLP, causal attention over a token block, chunked GDN, one bounded state transaction | Replace O(prompt tokens) host-driven full model steps; target TTFT first | Same-profile chunk/step parity or explicitly qualified chunk contract; no intermediate token publication |
| P2 | Efficient projection kernels/provider path, appropriate GEMV for decode and tensor-core GEMM for token/batch matrices | Improve actual arithmetic/memory throughput, not merely row count | Source codec/effective activation/output types and compute accumulation fixed; opaque workspace physically admitted |
| P3 | Fuse convolution+SiLU, Q/K normalize+coefficient preparation, gated RMS, residual+norm and SwiGLU where the profile permits | Reduce intermediate writes, launches and global synchronization | Preserve reference casts/reductions, finite checks and meaningful failure semantics |
| P4 | Reuse shape-bound scratch/commands; remove redundant scans/copies by constructing certified outputs and combining checks | Reduce certification, allocator and state-transport overhead | Retain required checks; one original authority, correct unknown-completion quarantine, no lease reuse before completion |
| P5 | Finish production CUDA graph admission and bounded decode graph replay | Reduce host overhead after the kernel structure is stable | Account for graph metadata, captured pointers/generations, all allocations/events and lifetime through retirement |
| P6 | Joint chunked prefill/decode scheduler, ragged refill, bounded overlap and per-tenant aging | Raise SLO goodput while controlling TTFT/ITL tails | Actual independent session/state/event ownership; no starvation or hidden dropped requests |
| P7 | Paged hybrid KV/GDN cache and exact complete-prefix reuse | Lower capacity/copy cost and exploit repeated work | Include recurrent/conv state, source/profile/tenant identity and causal frontier; cold no-hit baseline retained |
| P8 | Source-verified RAM/SSD/GPU streaming for capacity-bound27B | Enable the actual large model and overlap useful transfers | Stable source extents, bounded staging, true Ready events and physical resource accounting |
| P9 | Shape specialization and measured tuning of qualified kernels | Pursue a specific-device advantage after basic throughput is competitive | Offline bounded choices, held-out workload, no unbounded per-token JIT/search |
| P10 | Speculation/prefix combinations only after target execution is competitive | Additional useful committed tokens when acceptance pays for overhead | Exact target distribution/state rollback and full cost of rejected work; target-only comparison |

P1 has three distinct cuts: sequential T2/T4 amortizes gather/scatter,
readback and transaction overhead while repeating the mathematical body;
true temporal stateless lowering combines real teacher rows (including
solo B1/T2) across projections/MLP while respecting causal regions; the
fully qualified chunk attention/GDN path supplies larger temporal parallelism.
Measure each separately. A sequential loop is not token-matrix fusion.

For P2, preserve exact GGUF behavior by first investigating tiled/coalesced
weight loads, shared activation preparation and integer DP4A work within
the existing codec/block/lane reductions. Keep scale addition order and
overflow bounds. BF16 tensor-core GEMM belongs to the independently qualified
vLLM GPU profile; it is not a drop-in replacement for CPU-exact GGUF math.

Do not begin with speculative decoding to hide a slow or incorrect target.
Do not quantize the model/cache more aggressively and call the resulting
quality change a free speed improvement. Do not remove state isolation to
improve a benchmark.

Potential advantages over vLLM are hypotheses: lower host overhead on this
small GPU, efficient small-shape quantized kernels, fused state operations,
and workload-aware hybrid caching/scheduling. Promote only measured wins.

## 10. Two benchmark deliverables

### A. Model execution benchmark

Separate pure prefill and decode after a fixed prefix. Report model/source/
numeric profile, prompt length, teacher-input tokens/s separately from
generated/committed output tokens/s, per-step
latency, physical memory, kernel counts, transferred bytes and device time.
No HTTP/network overhead is attributed to kernels. A pure operator
microbenchmark remains a diagnostic, not the model result.

Preserve canonical47-input/8-output continuity. First admitted GPU matrix:
.8B and2B, B1/2/4/8, prompt lengths1/32/47/128/448 and output lengths8/64,
subject to the actual consumed-token frontier fitting capacity512.
Never run512 prompt plus32/128 generated tokens against that capacity or
silently truncate. After real capacity/numerical qualification, expand to
512/2048/8192 contexts and32/128 outputs within the enlarged envelope.
Cold-first-request and steady warm remain separate.
Add original27B only on a physically admitted, equivalent placement. Report
capacity-enabling streaming separately from resident performance.

### B. OpenAI serving benchmark

Use [serve-bench.py](../../../tools/serve-bench.py) and
[serve-compare.py](../../../tools/serve-compare.py). Preserve their existing
owned-provider lifecycle and alternating ABBA/BAAB sampling.

- Same exact source/quant, effective loader/numeric policy, tokenizer/template,
  raw IDs, generation/EOS/stop/sampling rules and output budget.
- Same device/driver, resource caps, power/thermal conditions and comparable
  residency/cache state; serialized arms on the shared GPU.
- Report startup separately from first request after readiness. Separate
  storage-cache cold, process cold, warmed model and prefix-cache hit/miss.
  One B1 warmup does not warm every B8/JIT/graph shape; declare an additional
  shape-warmed protocol symmetrically when that is what is measured.
- Compare eager routes for diagnosis and actual optimized/default vLLM V1
  routes for the competitive claim. Pin graph, prefix cache, chunked prefill,
  token/sequence budgets and attention/GDN backends.
- Start concurrency1/2/4/8 within current tool bounds. Use fixed open-loop
  arrival traces, short/long mixes and multiple tenants; sweep offered load
  through saturation. Expand concurrency only after admission/tool support.
  Workload labels alone measure class balance; authenticated tenant fairness
  additionally requires the actual tenant identity/admission boundary.
- Report offered/admitted/rejected/canceled/timed-out/completed requests,
  committed correct tokens, p50/p95/p99 TTFT and token ITL, SLO goodput,
  per-tenant completion/latency, memory and complete device counts.
- SSE chunk spacing is not individual-token ITL. When delivery coalesces,
  use authenticated token commit events for engine ITL; report client delivery
  independently and leave unavailable token-level measurements unset.

Current `serve-compare.py` deliberately leaves qualified source-correct
SLO-goodput null and equivalence `NOT_ESTABLISHED`; it also does not estimate
confidence intervals. The minimal follow-on is to bind an independently
accepted numerical qualification and physical commit evidence, then compute
paired statistics from retained raw runs. Merely supplying equal hashes or
matching generated text must not unlock that result.

Before measurement freeze workload/SLO/quality conditions. Retain the existing
10s TTFT/2s delivery-ITL workload as a historical comparator; define practical
interactive and long-prefill SLO classes separately before running them.
Use at least two balanced ABBA/BAAB cycles for screening. For promotion,
predeclare a larger fixed repeat budget, analyze independent run-level paired
ratios and95% confidence intervals, and do not treat correlated token samples
as independent repetitions.

**Win condition:** on a named qualified workload/hardware/configuration,
the95% confidence interval for correct committed SLO-goodput ratio is above1,
with no regression beyond predeclared latency, quality, rejection, completion
or fairness budgets. Report neutral/loss cases alongside wins. No engine-wide
“faster than vLLM” claim follows from one successful prompt or model.
If baseline goodput is zero, a ratio is undefined: use an absolute goodput
difference and its confidence interval, never an infinite-speedup claim.

## 11. Stop conditions and immediate next work

Stop promotion at the first incorrect tensor, incomplete state mapping,
unadmitted resource, unknown physical completion or missing independent
oracle. Continue diagnosis at that operation; do not advance a claim.

When the owner resumes implementation, the first concrete work is:

1. Revalidate paused overlays and accepted artifacts; use the existing bulk
   worktree for the bounded CPU reproduction.
2. Establish actual .8B vLLM projection→convolution inputs and select the
   first complete GDN layer's pinned phase/backend.
3. Port the smallest differing operation with genuine before/after evidence,
   immediately compose it, then walk forward to complete layer/state parity.
4. Expand to complete .8B,2B,27B and the parity matrix.
5. Implement temporal prefill and efficient projections before claiming that
   small launch reductions close the observed throughput gap.

The paused ordered-SiLU candidate remains unaccepted until its model/physical
gates pass. Do not use `target/release/zerogravity` as an accepted baseline
without checking which build produced it.
````

````markdown
## 2. Original user vision and architecture chronology — beginning to present

### 2.1 What Zerogravity is

A single Rust-native, composable AI execution fabric and eventually one deployable binary to run **text, image, video, audio, real-time and combined multimodal** inference locally and across trusted heterogeneous devices/peers. A simple Ollama-like single-model CLI should coexist with explicit power-user YAML configuration, many model registrations, a router, OpenAI-like APIs and advanced performance scheduling. Model mathematics, hardware-native kernels, memory placement and physical resource ownership specialize independently without forking the semantic/runtime engine. Strong source correctness, cancellation/state safety and real benchmarks take precedence over marketing claims.

Core inspirations/prior art to study (not automatically copy code): llama.cpp/GGUF and portable CPU source math; vLLM continuous batching/paged attention; SGLang cache/scheduled programs; Ollama UX; CubeCL (actually vendored upstream license); gufo, strata/maya, dwarfstar4/ds4, and extreme SSD/sparse execution; heterogeneous TPU/NPU/AMD/NVIDIA research. Project-authored code is MIT; model licenses and vendored upstream licenses are independent. Attribution, exact upstream versions and source-file provenance are required.

### 2.3 Latest owner decisions carried forward verbatim in substance

## 3. System ownership and critical invariants (do not fork these)

**Semantic truth:** immutable verified TensorSource/model definition and source-specific geometry/arithmetic/codec/source license; per-model exact tokenizer and runtime parameters. SourceIdentity issued once; a path or readonly mmap is not ownership of immutable bytes. Source bundle identity includes verified index plus each learned shard's SHA256, length and basename. Source-fingerprint mismatches refuse numerical comparison.

**Compilation:** one SemanticProgram/ForwardPlan and guarded typed operation/state/parameter/value schedule. ExecutableBundle binding, preflight, codegen, math/codec specialization and transient lowering views are not new inference engines. Source mathematical operations are authoritative; helper numerical scans must not become independent token loops. Qwen3.8 original analytic diagnostics are separate from trained and production paths until accepted.

**Logical state:** SessionAuthority alone issues RootBinding and root epochs. TaskCoordinator prepares private candidate state (KV/GDN/recurrent, token/grammar/RNG/index/media frontiers) and promotes it only after domain compatibility, complete device execution/readout and causal identity checks. A draft/token event/Ready proposal is not already committed. A canceled or stale proposal MUST NOT publish any root. Cross-request B>1 transaction first validates all rows and physical Ready, then obtains all original RootTransitions before any infallible swap.

**Physical state and safety:** one ResourceArbiter/process-shared physical admission authority, physical queue, BufferLease and device generation. Count actual overlapping VRAM/UMA/system memory once, preserve OS/cgroup headroom and driver allocator reality. Asynchronous Future abandonment is not hardware cancellation: do not reuse buffers, state or staging while completion is unknown. Retain/fence/quarantine and require real terminal events/readback. Model load, token work, transfer staging and output have distinct budget classes.

**Serving:** one route registry/admission and one shared resident model per canonical original source. Per-request queues, deadline/backpressure/cancel/state ownership and safe token/finish/usage responses. Router alias/profile selection is cold control work, not per-token content rewriting. Sessions are sticky to compatible source/provider; no unsafe hot migration, cross-session mutable KV or false OpenAI API claims. CPU and GPU share text output/greedy contract; GPU-only requested backend must fail closed.

**Numerical parity:** exact B1 original source F32/GGUF integer/FMA/reduction, BF16 source casts, GDN decay/softplus/sigmoid/beta, IMRoPE, canonical signed zero/future padded state, QK/softmax/AV, full vocab and every state domain. Operator bit parity, whole-model internal parity, independently trained framework parity, functional context and performance SLO are different gates. No unqualified tolerance relaxation or “training quality” inference from top-20 logits.

**Distributed and media:** remote peers and media task services prepare private changes under one coordinator; independent transport/ACK/playback semantics are not GPU root commits. Hosted service adapter has separate authorization, privacy, cost/idempotency and Unknown states, never counterfeit native kernel status.

For Nix split CUDA headers use scripts/cuda-nix-include-view.sh with already-installed CUDART_INCLUDE and CCCL_INCLUDE paths, set CUDA_PATH to its printed path, add compatible NVRTC + driver to LD_LIBRARY_PATH. Local smoke used existing CUDA 12.9 runtime/CCCL/NVRTC; without an include root CubeCL compiler previously panicked/retried and initial physical proof was invalid.     curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/models
````
